items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: His arrangers were like Frank Foster and Thad Jones and Jim Mundy, Nestico and I’m leaving out somebody.

ctx.x: But did you eventually get — you wrote something and then the band played it?

Oh no. That didn’t happen for maybe another two years from the first time I went to the front of the bus and showed Fos my arrangement, you know. And that was like passing out an arrangement to the Basie band was like going before the Supreme Court, you know? “Wow man I don’t know if this is going to work, man, this isn’t Basie. No, it’s not going to work, toss it.” It took me years, like what? Man. But the Basie band, that’s how they kept their sound. They were very strict as far as not letting just anything be…
